name: May
focus: Students home for the holidays + Mother's Day
objective: Students home from college fill empty off-peak seats; Mother's Day duos; keep April's buyers attending.
strategy:
Home for the Holidays.

Commercial job: Students home from college fill empty off-peak seats; Mother's Day duos; keep April's buyers attending.

Newcomer: Mom Said Get Off the Couch (“Home for the summer and Mom's already said 'do something'?”). Weekday 10–12 and weekend 4–7 pm run 27–41% full; the marginal cost of a seat there is near zero. Students arriving home in May are a predictable, untapped audience.

Newcomer: Group Project (Finally, Everyone Pulls Their Weight) (“Group projects: usually one person does all the work. Not here.”). Bulk purchase is one of the few places 25% is allowed. Groups attend together (higher usage → higher renewal) and bring four new names per sale.

Newcomer: Mom-entum (“She carried you for 9 months. You can carry her to class.”). Duos with a booked second class convert best; Mother's Day gives a reason. The perk is a shared session, not a bigger discount.

Renewal: Don't Ghost Us After the Party (“Great party. Now show up 8 times in May.”). 2026 anniversary-code buyers renewed at only 24.5%. Attendance in the month after purchase is the best predictor of renewal; the reward is earned by it.
notes: Build: 62 new buyers × ₹11,150 first-60-day spend = ₹6.9L; 68 renewals × ₹23,384 = ₹15.9L; 30 winbacks = ₹3.5L; privates/retail/drop-ins ₹2.6L. Offers carry ₹13.8L (48% of target); the rest is business-as-usual. Funnel uses measured rates (lead→trial 51% CRM status, trial→member 26.9%) — not invented lifts.

funnel.dataQuality: lead→trial = CRM 'Trial Completed' status (not attendance-verified); trial→member = trailing measured; see dataGaps
